title: Lust and Adultery of the Heart
searchTerms: Lust and Adultery of the Heart
definition: The doctrine of Lust and Adultery of the Heart teaches that jesus teaches that lust is not harmless imagination; it is heart-level adultery that treats people as objects for desire.
summary: Lust and Adultery of the Heart names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. Jesus teaches that lust is not harmless imagination; it is heart-level adultery that treats people as objects for desire. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to Lust and Adultery of the Heart because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: Jesus teaches that lust is not harmless imagination; it is heart-level adultery that treats people as objects for desire. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because secret sin forms the soul even when no one else sees it. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not make peace with hidden lust. Bring desire into the light, pursue purity with practical boundaries, and remember that Christ restores both the tempted and the broken. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
